window.note: "At evening" (no hour) to the order of 2.30 a. m., July 2 that follows the rest; the day bounds are used for the start (DD-LIFE-02)

place.text: a halt about 3 miles from Gettysburg

quote: At evening we halted about 3 miles from Gettysburg, and were ordered to build breastworks. Before the works were finished, we were ordered to rest. At 2.30 a. m., July 2, we were ordered to pack up quietly and cook coffee.
notes: Ordered to build breastworks at the evening halt; the works were not finished before the order to rest. Which materials and tools is not stated, so the clip is a stand-in. The report is Maj. Bradley's of 15 Aug. 1863 (proceedings from June 28).

window.note: dated by the paragraph "On the morning of the 3d, the Sixty-fourth was in line on the left of the brigade"; the hour is not stated; the first report (17 July, p. 405) repeats it as "a defense against the heavy cannonading"

place.text: to the front of the regiment, on the left of Brooke's brigade

quote: Breastworks were built to our front, which proved a protection against the heavy cannonading from the enemy on that day.
context_quote: On the morning of the 3d, the Sixty-fourth was in line on the left of the brigade
notes: Passive voice: who built them and with what is not stated; the regiment mustered 85 enlisted men with rifles that morning (same paragraph) but the passage does not say they all worked. The works took the cannonade of 3 July.

window.part_of_day: from dark on 12 July to the 13th
window.note: commenced "at dark" on the 12th (no hour), finished "on the 13th" (no hour): day bounds of the two stated days

place.text: a rocky ledge in a wood near Lapham's [Jones'] Cross-Roads, Md.

quote: At dark, commenced throwing iip intrenchments. On the 13th, we finished our breastworks.
context_quote: where we formed line of battle on the crest of a rocky ledge
notes: A second work of the regiment, in the line of battle before the Confederate position at the Potomac. Quote prints "iip" for up (OCR). Whether earth, stone or rails is not stated; the passage says "intrenchments" then "breastworks".

window.note: ordered at 2.30 a. m.; the regiment moved at 4.10 a. m. (the quote prints "4. 10")

place.text: the halt about 3 miles from Gettysburg

quote: At 2.30 a. m., July 2, we were ordered to pack up quietly and cook coffee. At 4. 10 a. m. we moved about 1 mile to the front
notes: Quiet cooking of coffee before a move at night: a camp-fire scene before dawn (sunrise 04:35 local mean time on 2 July by the project ephemeris). The order says to cook coffee; how and in what vessel is not stated.

window.note: the day is stated; the hour of the picket duty is not

place.text: on picket (position not stated), the regiment on the left of Brooke's brigade

quote: Our loss on the 3d was 1 man, wounded on picket, under the command of Capt. W. W. Wait.
notes: A picket detail of the regiment under Capt. W. W. Wait was out on 3 July; one man was wounded. Number of men on picket not stated.

place.text: the regiment's ground on the battlefield (place not stated)

quote: On the 4th we buried our dead
notes: The regiment buried its dead on 4 July; where and how (individual graves or trench) is not stated.

place.text: the regiment's ground on the battlefield (place not stated)

quote: held short religious services, conducted by Chaplain John H. W. Stuckenberg
context_quote: On the 4th we buried our dead and held short religious services
notes: Short religious services on 4 July conducted by the chaplain of the 145th Pennsylvania (Chaplain John H. W. Stuckenberg, as printed in the second report); the first report (p. 405) names no chaplain by name.

window.note: "Sunday morning, the 5th" is stated; the march followed at 4 p. m. (next sentence)

place.text: the regiment's ground on the battlefield (place not stated)

quote: On Sunday morning, the 5tli, I had an inspection of arms.
notes: Inspection of arms on the morning of 5 July: an assembled regiment standing in ranks; the clip is a stand-in. Quote prints "5tli" for 5th (OCR).

window.note: bivouacked at 8 p. m. at Two Taverns; the passage does not say when the bivouac broke (the next statement is "During the 6th, we remained in bivouac"): the end is the day bound

place.text: Two Taverns (on the Baltimore Pike, east of Gettysburg)

quote: At 4 p. m. marched with brigade in the direction of Frederick City ; bivouacked at 8 p. m. at Two Taverns.
notes: Bivouac for the night after a march of four hours; no fire, meal or camp layout is stated.

window.note: "During the 6th" (whole day); the place is the preceding sentence's Two Taverns

place.text: in bivouac at Two Taverns (by the preceding sentence)

quote: During the 6th, we remained in bivouac.
context_quote: bivouacked at 8 p. m. at Two Taverns
notes: A day in bivouac (a rest day after the march); nothing else of the day is stated. The place is carried from the previous sentence, not restated.

window.note: "On the 7th" (OCR "yth"); the hour of the issue is not stated

quote: On the yth, marched 9^ miles to near Taneytown; received rations
notes: Rations were received on arriving near Taneytown on 7 July; what was issued is not stated. The quote prints "yth" for 7th and "9^" for 9 1/2 (OCR).

window.note: "On the 7th" bivouacked near Taneytown; the next day's march began at 5 a. m. (stated): the end of the bivouac; the start is the day bound

quote: received rations and bivouacked. On the 8th, marched at 5 a. m.
notes: Bivouac of the night of 7-8 July; the window start is the day's start because no hour of arrival is stated (not an invented hour).

window.note: marched at 5 a. m. on the 8th; bivouacked "for the night" (no hour)

quote: Soon after moving, a hard rain came on, making the roads very muddy. This was a hard day's march for the men; bivouacked for the night near Frederick City.
notes: A hard rain fell on the march of 8 July (same passage); the passage does not say it rained in the bivouac.

window.part_of_day: marched at 5 a. m.; bivouacked (no hour)
window.note: the hour of the bivouac is not stated

place.text: near Crampton's Gap, Md. (bracketed in the print)

quote: July 9, marched at 5 a. m., Sixty-fourth leading the brigade; bivouacked near [Crampton's Gap], Md.
notes: The bracketed place name is the editor's correction in the printed report.

place.text: near Keedysville (Md.), after the line of battle

quote: On the 10th, moved at 5 a. m. ; crossed Antietam River at Keedysville; marched 3^ miles, and formed a line of battle; at night bivouackea.
notes: Quote prints "bivouackea" (OCR for bivouacked) and "3^" (3 1/2). No ocr_repairs needed: both are kept as printed.
